'''Cboe Global Markets, Inc.''' (formerly '''CBOE Holdings''' and '''Chicago Board Options Exchange''') is an American financial [[Exchange (organized market)|exchange]] operator.<ref name=10K/> In the U.S., it owns the largest exchange for trading in [[Option (finance)|option]]s, where it has a 30% market share, and the third-largest exchange for trading in equities (after the [[New York Stock Exchange]] and the [[Nasdaq]]), where it has a 10% market share.<ref name=10K/> It operates the largest stock exchange in Europe, where it has a 25% market share.<ref name=10K/> It is headquartered in [[Chicago]], where it maintains an [[open outcry]] trading floor.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/business/2022/6/6/23156813/cboe-global-markets-trading-floor-open-outcry | title='Open outcry' trading cranks up the volume at Chicago's equity options market, 'open outcry' cranks up the volume | first=David | last=Roeder | work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] | date=June 6, 2022}}</ref> 

The company offers trading in options on both [[stock market index]]es and individual stocks (52% of 2025 revenues), North American equities via its ownership of BZX, BYX, EDGX, and EDGA (35% of 2025 revenues), Europe and Asia Pacific equities (8% of 2025 revenues), [[futures contract]]s on the [[VIX]] (3% of 2025 revenues), and trading in [[foreign exchange market]]s (2% of 2025 revenues).<ref name=10K/>

==History==
===1969-1973: Background===
In 1969, the vice chairman of the Chicago Board of Trade, Edmund "Eddie" O'Connor, developed the idea for an options exchange.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.ft.com/content/e5289224-2282-11e0-b6a2-00144feab49a | title=Chicago Board Options Exchange founder dies | last=Grant | first=Jeremy | work=[[Financial Times]] | date=January 17, 2011 | url-access=subscription}}</ref> At that time, options on stocks were traded in a New York-based,<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.tradersmagazine.com/departments/options/book-notethe-birth-of-the-cboe/ | title=Book Note:The Birth of The CBOE | work=Traders Magazine | date=June 23, 2011}}</ref> over-the-counter market which required a direct link between the buyer and seller and complex terms of sale.<ref name=Thriving>{{cite news | url=https://www.barrons.com/articles/SB50001424052748703889404578438860106833412 | title=40 Years Later, CBOE Is Thriving | last=McMillan | first=Lawrence | work=[[Barron's]] | date=April 27, 2013 | url-access=subscription}}</ref> The options exchange that O'Connor imagined would use a central clearinghouse to facilitate and guarantee trades and contracts.<ref name=Thriving/> The Chicago Board of Trade established a committee to evaluate the concept.<ref name=advent/>

The options market idea faced resistance from officials at the [[United States Securities and Exchange Commission]].<ref name=Create>{{cite news | url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/joseph-sullivan-iii-helped-create-chicago-options-exchange-11602788431 | title=Joseph Sullivan III Helped Create Chicago Options Exchange | date=October 15, 2020 | last=Hagerty | first=James R. | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | url-access=subscription}}</ref> The CBOT hired Joseph Sullivan to address regulator concerns and present the concept to the New York brokerage community.<ref name=Thriving/> In October 1971, the SEC relented and approved the effort.<ref name=advent>{{cite web | url=https://www.sechistorical.org/collection/papers/2010/2019_02_08_CBOE_Joe%20Sullivan.pdf | title=THE ADVENT OF THE CHICAGO BOARD OPTIONS EXCHANGE: A GOLDEN ANNIVERSARY MEMOIR BY ITS FOUNDING PRESIDENT Joe Sullivan}}</ref>

In February 1972, the Chicago Board Options Exchange was incorporated as an independent body with its own bylaws and governing board.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/news/ct-xpm-1993-04-26-9304260251-story.html | title=Maturing CBOE confident at 20 | last=Crawford | first=William B. | work=[[Chicago Tribune]] | date=April 26, 1993}}</ref> Joseph Sullivan became the president of the organization.<ref name=Create/> 

===1973: Launch===
Founded by the [[Chicago Board of Trade]] in 1973 and member-owned for several decades, the Chicago Board Options Exchange was the first exchange to list standardized, exchange-traded stock options. Its first day of trading was on April 26, 1973, in celebration of the 125th birthday of the Chicago Board of Trade.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://static.moaf.org/docs/Cboe%2050th%20Anniversary.pdf | title=Cboe Marks Golden Anniversary | first=Howard | last=Baker | work=[[Museum of American Finance]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1973/04/27/archives/trading-in-options-opens-on-new-chicago-board-openingday-options.html | title=Trading in Options Opens On New Chicago Board | first=H. J. | last=Maidenberg | work=[[The New York Times]] | date=April 27, 1973 | url-access=limited}}</ref> Trading was conducted in the former CBOT smoking lounge.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2020/10/13/21515023/joseph-sullivan-iii-founding-president-chicago-board-options-exchange | title=Joseph Sullivan III, founding president of Chicago Board Options Exchange, dies at 82 | last=Roeder | first=David | work=[[Chicago Sun Times]] | date=October 13, 2020 }}</ref> In its first full month of operation, 34,599 contracts were traded. By 1976, the monthly volume of trades had increased to 1.5 million.<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-financial-and-quantitative-analysis/article/abs/chicago-board-options-exchange-and-market-efficiency/DAD99A2DD11828307A132815D9FAEA3F | last=Finnerty | first=Joseph E. | date=1978 | title=The Chicago board options exchange and market efficiency | journal=[[Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis]] | volume=13 |issue=1 | pages=29–38 | doi=10.2307/2330518 | jstor=2330518 | hdl=2027.42/35606 | hdl-access=free | url-access=subscription }}</ref>

===1977-2009: New headquarters and VIX===
Over the next decade, CBOE continued to operate from its location within the CBOT building. In 1984, CBOE moved to its next headquarters across the street at 400 S. LaSalle Street.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.chicagobusiness.com/commercial-real-estate/cboe-confirms-hq-move-chicago-old-post-office | title=Cboe confirms HQ move to Old Post Office | last=Marek | first=Lynne | work=[[Crain's Chicago Business]] | date=September 17, 2019 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

On January 19, 1993, CBOE introduced the CBOE Volatility Index ([[VIX]]), created by [[Robert E. Whaley]], a finance professor at [[Vanderbilt University]], to measure 30-day implied volatility of [[S&P 100]] options.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.businessinsider.com/vix-creator-bob-whaley-interview-investors-dont-understand-wall-street-fear-gauge-2017-9 | title=The creator of Wall Street's 'fear gauge' says people don't understand it as well as they should | last=Rapier | first=Graham | work=[[Business Insider]] | date=September 11, 2017}}</ref> In 2003, the underlying benchmark for the VIX was changed to the [[S&P 500]].<ref name=oralhistory>{{cite news | url=https://www.ft.com/content/5c840fbe-9949-43ab-9058-633023031582 | last=Wigglesworth | first=Robin | title=An oral history of the fear index | work=[[Financial Times]] | date=September 20, 2023 | url-access=subscription}}</ref> The company launched tradable products using VIX as the underlying index, including [[futures contract]]s on the VIX, launched in 2004 after a survey of [[Goldman Sachs]] salespeople showed interest in the product.<ref name=oralhistory/>

===2010-present: IPO and acquisitions ===
In June 2010, the company became a [[public company]] via an [[initial public offering]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2010/06/15/cboe-garners-339-million-in-ipo/ | title=CBOE garners $339 million in IPO | first=Michael | last=O'Neal | work=[[Chicago Tribune]] | date=June 15, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/06/16/business/16options.html | title=CBOE Shares Jump in Market Debut | agency=[[Reuters]] | work=[[The New York Times]] | date=June 16, 2010 | url-access=limited}}</ref>

In December 2011, CBOE Stock Exchange, which was owned by CBOE Holdings, acquired the [[National Stock Exchange (Jersey City, New Jersey)|National Stock Exchange]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/business/ct-xpm-2011-09-29-chi-cboe-stock-market-to-acquire-allelectronic-stock-exchange-20110929-story.html/ | title=CBOE stock market to acquire all-electronic stock exchange | work=[[Chicago Tribune]] | date=September 29, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.tradersmagazine.com/news/national-stock-exchange-set-to-close-december-16/ |title=National Stock Exchange Set to Close December 16 | work=Traders Magazine | date=December 13, 2016}}</ref> It ceased trading operations on May 30, 2014.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2014-05-02/national-stock-exchange-files-with-sec-to-halt-operations.html | title=National Stock Exchange Files With SEC to Halt Operations | first=Sam | last=Mamudi | work=[[Bloomberg News]] | date=May 2, 2014 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In August 2015, CBOE acquired the LiveVol trading analytics platforms, including Livevol Core, Livevol Pro, and Livevol X.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.hedgeweek.com/cboe-holdings-acquires-livevol/ | title=CBOE Holdings acquires Livevol |work=Hedge Week |date=August 10, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite press release | url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/cboe-holdings-to-acquire-data-and-analytics-platforms-of-livevol-inc-300092512.html | title=CBOE Holdings To Acquire Data And Analytics Platforms Of Livevol, Inc. | publisher=[[PR Newswire]] | date=June 2, 2015}}</ref> Livevol X was sold to Sterling Trading Tech in March 2017.<ref>{{cite press release | url=https://sterlingtradingtech.com/news-insights/sterling-trading-tech-acquire-cboes-livevol-x-trading-platform | title=Sterling Trading Tech to Acquire CBOE’s Livevol X Trading Platform | publisher=Sterling Trading Tech | date=March 21, 2017}}</ref>

In January 2016, CBOE purchased a majority stake in Vest Financial, an investment adviser specializing in options-centric products.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.chicagobusiness.com/article/20160125/NEWS01/160129904/cboe-buys-majority-stake-in-vest-financial | title=CBOE buys majority stake in options trading software firm | last=Marek | first=Lynne | work=[[Crain's Chicago Business]] | date=January 25, 2016 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In March 2017, CBOE acquired BATS Global Markets, second-largest US stock exchange by shares traded, for approximately US$3.2 billion.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.bizjournals.com/kansascity/news/2017/03/01/cboe-bats-merger-staff-changes.html | title=With CBOE deal done, here's what Bats looks like now | first=James | last=Dornbrook | work=[[American City Business Journals]] | date=March 1, 2017 | url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://fortune.com/2016/09/26/cboe-acquires-bats/ | title=CBOE Will Acquire BATS Global Markets for $3.2 Billion | agency=[[Reuters]] | work=[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]] | date=September 26, 2016 | url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/cboe-holdings-to-buy-bats-for-3-2-billion-1474890580 | title=CBOE, Bats Deal Creates New Exchange Behemoth | last1=Hope | first1=Bradley | last2=Demos | first2=Telis |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | date=September 26, 2016 | url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.businessinsider.com/cboe-to-buy-bats-global-markets-for-32-billion-2016-9 | title=2 of the biggest exchange groups in the US have agreed to merge | last=Oyedele | first=Akin | work=[[Business Insider]] | date=September 26, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.thetradenews.com/cboe-completes-3-4-billion-bats-acquisition/ | title=CBOE completes $3.4 billion Bats acquisition | last=McDowell | first=Hayley | work=The Trade | date=March 1, 2017}}</ref> Over the next few years, CBOE migrated its exchanges onto the BATS technology platform.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.thetradenews.com/cboe-global-markets-finalises-migration-bats-technology/ | title=Cboe Global Markets finalises migration to Bats technology | last=Brazier | first=John | work=The Trade News | date=October 9, 2019}}</ref>

In October 2017, the company rebranded from CBOE Holdings to Cboe Global Markets.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.hedgeweek.com/cboe-holdings-unveils-new-corporate-identity/ |title=CBOE Holdings unveils new corporate identity |work=Hedge Week |date=October 17, 2017}}</ref>

In August 2018, the company delisted from the [[Nasdaq]] and listed its shares on its own exchange.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.ft.com/content/75db86b4-9698-11e8-b67b-b8205561c3fe |title=Cboe Global Markets to list shares exclusively on its own exchange |last=Bullock |first=Nicole |work=[[Financial Times]] |date=August 2, 2018 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In September 2019, CBOE relocated its headquarters to the [[Old Chicago Main Post Office]] and began construction of a new trading floor in the Chicago Board of Trade building, which was the space the exchange originally occupied in the 1970s and 1980s.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2019/9/17/20870495/cboe-chicago-board-options-exchange-headquarters-trading-floor-move-post-office |last=Roeder |first=David |title=Chicago options exchange to move headquarters, open new trading floor |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |date=September 17, 2019}}</ref> The new trading floor opened in June 2022.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-06-06/cboe-keeps-old-school-pit-alive-with-new-chicago-trading-floor |last=Doherty |first=Katherine |title=Cboe Keeps Old Model Alive Opening New Trading Floor |work=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=June 6, 2022 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In February 2020, Cboe acquired two data analytics firms, Hanweck and FT Options.<ref>{{cite press release | url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/cboe-global-markets-acquires-data-analytics-companies-hanweck-and-ft-options-300998333.html | title=Cboe Global Markets Acquires Data Analytics Companies Hanweck and FT Options | publisher=[[PR Newswire]] | date=February 4, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.reuters.com/article/markets/europe/cboe-global-markets-acquires-data-analytics-companies-hanweck-and-ft-options-idUSASA00BS4/ | title=CBOE Global Markets Acquires Data Analytics Companies Hanweck And Ft Options | work=[[Reuters]] | date=February 4, 2020}}</ref>

In May 2020, the company expanded into Canada via the acquisition of MATCHNow, which operated an [[alternative trading system]] (ATS).<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-virtu-fincl-m-a-cboe/cboe-to-buy-virtus-matchnow-dark-pool-to-expand-into-canada-idINKBN22V1ST/ |title=Cboe to buy Virtu's MATCHNow dark pool to expand into Canada |last=McCrank |first=John |work=[[Reuters]] |date=May 19, 2020}}</ref>

In June 2020, CBOE acquired Trade Alert, a New York-based order flow analysis service provider.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.thetradenews.com/cboe-adds-real-time-trade-alerts-and-data-with-latest-acquisition/ |title=Cboe adds real-time trade alerts and data with latest acquisition |last=McDowell |first=Hayley |work=The Trade News | date=June 2, 2020}}</ref> 

In July 2020, Cboe acquired the remaining 80% of [[EuroCCP]], a Dutch clearing house, that it did not already own.<ref>{{Cite press release | url=https://www.prnewswire.co.uk/news-releases/cboe-global-markets-completes-euroccp-acquisition-plans-to-launch-cboe-europe-derivatives-in-first-half-of-2021-889218037.html | title=Cboe Global Markets Completes EuroCCP Acquisition, Plans to Launch Cboe Europe Derivatives in First Half of 2021 | publisher=[[PR Newswire]] | date=July 1, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSKBN1YE0K3/ | title=Cboe buys EuroCCP to bolster Dutch EU base after Brexit |last=Jones |first=Huw |work=[[Reuters]] | date=December 10, 2019}}</ref> 

Cboe acquired another ATS operator, BIDS Trading, in October 2020.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bizjournals.com/chicago/news/2020/10/16/cboe-buys-block-trading-firm-bids-trading.html |title=Cboe buys block-trading firm BIDS Trading |last=Miller |first=Ben |work=[[American City Business Journals]] | date=October 19, 2020 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In June 2021, Cboe acquired Chi-X Asia Pacific, which owned exchanges in Japan and Australia.<ref>{{Cite press release | url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/cboe-global-markets-completes-acquisition-of-chi-x-asia-pacific-301323750.html | title=Cboe Global Markets Completes Acquisition of Chi-X Asia Pacific | publisher=[[PR Newswire]] | date=June 30, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-03-24/cboe-buys-chi-x-asia-pacific-expanding-into-japan-australia |last1=Ossinger |title=Cboe Buys Chi-X Asia Pacific to Expand Into Japan, Australia |first1=Joanna |last2=Ahmed |first2=Nabila |work=[[Bloomberg News]] |date=March 24, 2021 | url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/cboe-stock-exchange-expands-into-asia-broaden-market-data-2021-03-25/ | title=Cboe stock exchange expands into Asia to broaden market data | first1=Huw | last1=Jones | first2=Rashmi | last2=Ashok | editor-first=Shinjini | editor-last=Ganguli | work=[[Reuters]] | date=March 25, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.theaustralian.com.au/business/cboe-to-give-asx-a-run-for-its-money/news-story/e772c5b702e9cf94c6985a4b94f93966 |title=Cboe to give ASX a run for its money |last=Durie |first=John |work=[[The Australian]] |date=January 18, 2022}}</ref> 

In November 2021, Cboe acquired NEO, a Canadian stock exchange operator, which was rebranded as [[Cboe Canada]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/bourse-operator-cboe-buy-canadas-neo-exchange-2021-11-15/ |title=Bourse operator Cboe to buy Canada's NEO exchange |last=McCrank |first=John |work=[[Reuters]] |date=November 15, 2021}}</ref>

In May 2022, Cboe acquired Eris Digital Holdings (ErisX), a US-based [[digital asset]] [[spot market]], regulated [[futures contract]]s exchange, and regulated [[Clearinghouse model|clearinghouse]], which was renamed CBOE Digital.<ref>{{Cite press release | url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/cboe-global-markets-completes-acquisition-of-erisx-entering-digital-asset-market-301537549.html | title=Cboe Global Markets Completes Acquisition of ErisX, Entering Digital Asset Market | publisher=[[PR Newswire]] | date=May 2, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.chicagobusiness.com/finance-banking/cryptocurrency-future-cme-terry-duffy-cboe-ed-tilly | last=Daniels | first=Steve | title=What does the crypto collapse mean for Chicago's exchanges? | work=[[Crain's Chicago Business]] | date=December 13, 2022 | url-access=subscription}}</ref> The company took a $460 million writedown on the investment shortly thereafter.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.reuters.com/business/exchange-operator-cboes-profit-rises-trading-volumes-surge-2022-07-29/ | title=Exchange operator Cboe writes down bulk of ErisX acquisition | first1=Manya | last1=Saini | first2=John | last2=McCrank | editor-first1=Shailesh | editor-last1=Kuber | editor-first2=Matthew | editor-last2=Lewis | work=[[Reuters]] | date=July 29, 2022}}</ref>

In September 2023, CEO Edward Tilly resigned after failing to disclose personal relationships with colleagues.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.ft.com/content/0a9b5138-5d27-4ea2-8616-4c16baf1883c | title=Cboe chief resigns over undisclosed relationships with colleagues | last1=Hughes |first1=Jennifer | last2=Chávez | first2=Steff | work=[[Financial Times]] | date=September 19, 2023 | url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/us/cboe-ceo-tilly-resigns-over-personal-relationships-with-colleagues-2023-09-19/ | title=Cboe CEO resigns over personal relationships, stock gains 3% | first1=Jaiveer | last1=Shekhawat | first2=Laura | last2=Matthews | work=[[Reuters]] | date=September 19, 2023}}</ref>

In September 2024, the company partnered with Globacap to create a U.S. trading platform for shares of closely held companies.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/cboe-partners-with-uk-firm-launch-us-private-share-trading-platform-bloomberg-2024-09-05/ | title=CBOE partners with UK firm to launch U.S. private share trading platform, Bloomberg News reports | first1=Jaiveer Singh | last1=Shekhawat | first2=Niket | last2=Nishant | editor-first=Tasim | editor-last=Zahid | work=[[Reuters]] | date=September 5, 2024}}</ref>

Fredric Tomczyk, CEO from 2023 to 2025, was succeeded by Craig Donohue in May 2025.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/money/2025/05/01/craig-donohue-tieup-two-chicago-exchanges-ceo-cboe-global-markets | title=Craig Donohue, who steered a tieup of two Chicago exchanges, named CEO of Cboe Global Markets | last=Roeder | first=David | work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] | date=May 1, 2025}}</ref> 

In August 2025, the company shut its operations in Japan.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.reuters.com/business/finance/cboe-global-exit-japan-equities-operations-2025-07-23/ | title=Cboe Global to exit Japan equities operations | first=Prakhar | last=Srivastava | editor-first=Devika | editor-last=Syamnath | work=[[Reuters]] | date=July 23, 2025}}</ref>

In April 2026, the company agreed to sell its Canadian and Australian equities businesses to [[TMX Group]] for US$300 million.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.dentons.com/en/insights/alerts/2026/april/28/tmx-group-limited-announces-agreement-to-acquire-cboe-australia-and-cboe-canada | title=TMX Group Limited announces agreement to acquire Cboe Australia and Cboe Canada from Cboe Global Markets, Inc. | work=[[Dentons]] | date=April 28, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/cboe-sell-canada-australia-exchanges-tmx-2026-04-22/ | title=Toronto exchange operator to buy Cboe's Canada, Australia units | first1=Anirban | last1=Sen | first2=Prakhar | last2=Srivastava | editor-first=Nivedita | editor-last=Bhattacharjee | work=[[Reuters]] | date=April 22, 2026}}</ref>

In May 2026, the company laid off 20% of its staff.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.wsj.com/business/cboe-is-slashing-20-of-its-staff-in-bid-to-focus-on-core-businesses-4be8b332 | title=Cboe Is Slashing 20% of Its Staff in Bid to Focus on Core Businesses | first=Krystal | last=Hur | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | date=May 1, 2026 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In June 2026, in partnership with [[Charles Schwab Corporation]], the company began work on yes-or-no options contracts tied to the performance of the [[S&P 500]].<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.wsj.com/finance/charles-schwab-breaks-into-the-prediction-market-business-61f6b9c2 | title=Charles Schwab Breaks Into the Prediction Market Business | first=Hannah Erin | last=Lang | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | date=June 19, 2026 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==Legal and regulatory issues==
===Abusive short selling===
In 2013, the company paid a $6 million penalty and implemented "major remedial measures" to settle charges that it failed to properly enforce rules to prevent abusive short selling.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.bizjournals.com/chicago/news/2013/06/11/cboe-to-pay-6-million-in-sec.html | title=CBOE to pay $6 million in SEC settlement | work=[[American City Business Journals]] | date=June 11, 2013 | url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424127887323495604578539372093768126 | title=SEC Alleges 'Systemic' Lapses in Oversight at CBOE | first1=Scott | last1=Patterson | first2=Jacob | last2=Bunge | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | date=June 11, 2013 | url-access=subscription}}</ref>

===Alleged patent infringement===
In 2007, the [[International Securities Exchange]] (ISE) sued CBOE, alleging that the company infringed on ISE's patent for "Automated Exchange for Trading Derivative Securities".<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.reuters.com/article/markets/ise-files-patent-infringement-lawsuit-against-cboe-idUSN06478167/ | title=ISE files patent infringement lawsuit against CBOE | first=Doris | last=Frankel | work=[[Reuters]] | date=August 9, 2007}}</ref> The judge sided with CBOE, and after ISE continued to litigate, in 2016, ISE was ordered to pay $6 million to CBOE for attorneys fees.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://www.fr.com/news/fish-wins-over-6-million-attorneys-fees-cboe-04-04-2016/ | title=Fish & Richardson Wins Over $6 Million in Attorneys' Fees for Chicago Board Options Exchange in Multi-Year Patent Dispute With ISE | work=[[Fish & Richardson]] | date=April 4, 2016}}</ref>

===Complaint against former director===
In 2024, William Carlson, founder of Belvedere Trading, filed a complaint with the Illinois Attorney Registration and Disciplinary Commission (ARDC) against Mark Francis Duffy, a former director at CBOE Global Markets. Carlson alleged that Duffy did not act on significant evidence of financial misconduct at Belvedere Trading while working as both the firm's legal counsel and a CBOE director. The complaint further suggested that Duffy's dual role may have hindered regulatory oversight and contributed to continued financial irregularities at the company.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://chicagocitywire.com/stories/671724953-belvedere-trading-dispute-resurfaces-as-founder-targets-former-cboe-director-in-ardc-complaint |title=Belvedere Trading dispute resurfaces as founder targets former CBOE director in ARDC complaint | work=Chicago City Wire |date=May 28, 2025}}</ref> In June 2025, Carson publicly accused individuals associated with Belvedere and Cboe of participating in a $35 million equity fraud and [[cover-up]] scheme. In a police complaint and related filings, Carlson alleged that Duffy was made aware of the misconduct as early as 2011 but failed to act despite being compensated to review the case. Carlson also claimed that Belvedere Trading, a Cboe member firm, and several implicated individuals were Cboe members, raising concerns about potential [[conflicts of interest]] and lapses in Cboe's self-regulatory oversight.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://chicagocitywire.com/stories/673089729-founder-of-belvedere-trading-llc-on-cboe-ties-belvedere-wrongdoers-are-all-mostly-cboe-members |title=Founder of Belvedere Trading LLC on CBOE ties: 'Belvedere wrongdoers are all mostly CBOE members' | work=Chicago City Wire | date=June 13, 2025}}</ref>

extract:
Cboe Global Markets, Inc. (formerly CBOE Holdings and Chicago Board Options Exchange) is an American financial exchange operator. In the U.S., it owns the largest exchange for trading in options, where it has a 30% market share, and the third-largest exchange for trading in equities (after the New York Stock Exchange and the Nasdaq), where it has a 10% market share. It operates the largest stock exchange in Europe, where it has a 25% market share. It is headquartered in Chicago, where it maintains an open outcry trading floor. 
The company offers trading in options on both stock market indexes and individual stocks (52% of 2025 revenues), North American equities via its ownership of BZX, BYX, EDGX, and EDGA (35% of 2025 revenues), Europe and Asia Pacific equities (8% of 2025 revenues), futures contracts on the VIX (3% of 2025 revenues), and trading in foreign exchange markets (2% of 2025 revenues).
